title: Propose to Learn, Learn to Propose: Evaluability-Aware Assistance under Bounded Rationality
abstract: arXiv:2609.02242v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI assistants often collaborate by proposing candidate edits, plans, or designs that users evaluate before adoption. Existing assistance methods focus on proposal quality or user-goal inference, often assuming that the user can reliably evaluate any proposal, which can fail in practice because of bounded rationality. We study evaluability-aware proposal planning, where proposals serve both as task interventions and as probes for learning latent preferences and evaluation constraints, where the resulting belief updates then guide later proposals. We formalise this setting as ProSE, a hidden-parameter sequential assistance problem, and instantiate it with a KL-regularised bounded-rational binary response model in which acceptance trades off value gain against a distance-dependent evaluability penalty. translated_title: 提议以学习，学习以提议：有界理性下的可评估性感知辅助
translated_abstract: AI助手常常通过提出候选的编辑、计划或设计方案来与用户协作，用户会先对这些方案进行评估再决定是否采纳。现有的辅助方法主要关注提案质量或用户目标推断，往往假设用户能够可靠地评估任何提案，但由于人类的有限理性，这一假设在实践中可能失效。我们研究了可评估性感知的提案规划问题，其中提案既作为任务干预手段，也作为探针用于学习用户的潜在偏好与评估约束，由此产生的信念更新进而指导后续提案的生成。我们将该问题形式化为ProSE——一个隐参数序贯辅助问题，并用一个KL正则化的有界理性二元响应模型对其进行实例化，其中用户是否接受提案，是价值收益与随距离衰减的可评估性惩罚之间权衡的结果。对该似然模型的规划后果进行分析后发现，最可能被用户接受的提案与信息量最大的探针并不一定重合……
tldr: 该论文提出可评估性感知的辅助框架ProSE，将AI助手的提案同时视为任务干预与探测用户评估能力的探针，并揭示“最可能被接受的提案”与“最有信息量的探针”并不一致这一关键权衡。
en_tdlr: This paper formalizes evaluability-aware assistance (ProSE), in which an AI assistant's proposals serve both as task interventions and as probes for learning the user's evaluation constraints, revealing that the most likely accepted proposals need not coincide with the most informative probes.
